title: Adaptive asymmetric-flow batcher: dynamic thresholds & KV tiling for skewed prompt/response workloads
creator: Priya Nambiar
description: Problem: customer production traces show a large fraction of sessions with highly asymmetric prompt->response length distributions (short prompts, very long responses and vice-versa). Our current continuous-batching scheduler treats length variance symmetrically which causes: p95 latency spikes for long responses, elevated KV cache fragmentation on GPUs, and suboptimal packing that wastes activation memory. Goal: build a runtime scheduler and KV-allocator that adapts batching thresholds and memory tiling per-length-profile to reduce p95 latency, reduce GPU memory fragmentation, and improve overall throughput under skewed dialogs.
acceptance_criteria: p95 generation latency for asymmetric workloads reduced by >=25% vs baseline on same infra
GPU activation + KV memory fragmentation metric reduced by >=30% (measured by free-contiguous-blocks gauge)
No regression (<=5%) on average latency and throughput for balanced workloads
Changes guarded behind runtime feature flag and can be toggled per-customer
Automated integration test that exercises short-prompt long-response and long-prompt short-response scenarios added to CI
progress_updates: 2026-03-08: Spike completed — profiled 18M requests from production (last 30 days). Identified 42% of sessions have >4x prompt/response asymmetry.

2026-03-09: Implemented prototype: asymmetric-flow controller that maintains two micro-queues (prompt-heavy and response-heavy) and dynamically adjusts batch thresholds based on recent per-queue latency pressure.

2026-03-10: KV tiling experiment added — instead of placing KV entries in first-fit slab, we group KV entries by predicted continuation length to improve locality; reduced scatter in allocator traces.
2026-03-11: End-to-end benchmark on p3.2xlarge-like nodes: baseline p95=1.8s, prototype p95=1.27s on long-response skew (29% improvement); memory fragmentation metric down 34% on sample workload.

2026-03-12: Running extended 24h soak in staging with mixed-tenancy; observed a pathological case where many small responses congest prompt-heavy queue — added backpressure heuristics and per-tenant soft quotas.
decisions: Use two logical flow classes (prompt-heavy, response-heavy) rather than N-length buckets to keep scheduler overhead low.
KV tiling will be implemented as a lightweight metadata tag on allocations (tile_id = predicted_response_bucket) to avoid introducing a new allocator layer.
Eviction policy: horizon-based preemptive eviction for tiles predicted to have low reuse probability; fallback to LRU within tile to preserve recent context.
Expose three knobs in runtime: max_batch_threshold_per_flow, tile_compaction_interval_ms, per_tenant_memory_soft_quota. Default safe values applied for hosted customers.
Feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.asymm_flow_v1 and rollout via canary route in Console.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: misprediction of continuation length could increase eviction churn. Mitigation: conservative predictions initially (coarse-grain buckets) and telemetry-driven tuning.
Risk: added scheduler complexity may increase tail latency under extreme load. Mitigation: implement fast-path that bypasses flow-splitting when queue sizes exceed emergency threshold.
Risk: per-tenant soft quotas could affect noisy neighbors. Mitigation: autoscaling overrides for Dedicated customers and dashboard alerting for quota hits.
experiments: Exp-001: compare two-queue asymm controller vs baseline across three synthetic distributions (short->long, long->short, uniform). Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU free-contiguous-blocks, throughput.
Exp-002: KV tiling size sweep (1,2,4 buckets) to measure trade-off between locality and tile management overhead.
Exp-003: Tile compaction interval sweep (100ms, 500ms, 2s) to find sweet spot for memory defragmentation without blocking serving threads.
